title: Pop’s on Top, But Other Genres Have Narrowed the Gap: State of the Hot 100’s Top 10 at Midyear 2026
summary: Here's a look at key trends in the chart's top 10 over the first half of the year, as analyzed by Hit Songs Deconstructed.
contentText:
What were some of the most notable trends on the Billboard Hot 100 songs chart during the first half of the year?

Hit Songs Deconstructed , which provides compositional analytics for top 10 Hot 100 hits, has released its midyear 2026 State of the Hot 100 Top 10 report.

Here are three takeaways from Hit Songs Deconstructed’s latest in-depth research.

Pop’s on Top, But Other Genres Are Gain ing

Pop reigned as the most common primary genre in the Hot 100’s top 10 throughout the first six months of 2026, contributing to 33% of all top 10s. It led with a 42% share for all of 2025, after claiming 29% in 2024.

Hip-hop/rap placed second with a 21% take over January-June, up from 19% in 2025, though markedly off its 38% showing in 2024. Its representation by midyear is a result “entirely of Drake material,” per Hit Songs Deconstructed’s report, as nine new top 10s in May from his album ICEMAN extended his record career count to 90.

Courtesy Hit Songs Deconstructed

Plus, “Country, dance/club/electronic, Latin and rock each held a 10% share” in the first half of 2026, “followed by R&B/soul at 7%,” the recap reveals. “Dance/club/electronic, Latin and rock all rose in prominence compared to 2025,” with Latin, notably, climbing to its highest share of the past five years, led by Bad Bunny .

Powering pop’s triumphs in 2026, among others: Hot 100 No. 1s for Taylor Swift , Ariana Grande and BTS .

Solo Vocals Soar

“Songs with a solo lead vocalist rose for the fifth straight year, to 86%, the highest level in over a decade,” Hit Songs Deconstructed finds. That command at midyear 2026 is up from 77% in 2025, 70% in 2024, 66% in 2023 and 62% in 2022.

As for gender splits, “Male-led songs rose to 57%, female-led songs declined to 36% and only 7% of songs featured a male/female duet,” according to the research. That tracks with much of the decade, with male-led Hot 100 top 10s ranging from 49% to 58% since 2022 and women-led hits between 31% and 42%.

Echoing hip-hop/rap’s regression in the top 10 since 2024, “Exclusively sung lead vocal deliveries remained in the majority for the fourth straight year, at 62%,” Hit Songs Deconstructed noted, “while exclusively rapped deliveries were absent for the first time since 2015.”

Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Deconstructed: Heartbreak That Feels Authentic & Relatable

Love Is in Bloom

What themes are connecting with listeners so far this year?

“Love/relationships remained the dominant lyrical focus, appearing in 69% of top 10 hits during first the half of 2026, up slightly from 67% 2025,” Hit Songs Deconstructed reported. “Within that broader theme, romantic/being love subject matter rose to 57%, its highest level in over a decade.”

Among leading love songs, spanning various matters of the heart, that have hit the Hot 100’s top 10 this year: Swift’s “Opalite,” Olivia Dean ’s “So Easy (To Fall in Love),” Bruno Mars ’ “I Just Might,” Harry Styles ’ “American Girls” and Ella Langley ’s 15-weeks-and-counting No. 1, “Choosin’ Texas.”
